title: Detuning-robust Rydberg entangling gates from echoed pulses
authors: Zhubing Jia, Yichao Yu, Xiye Hu, Lintao Li, Jacob Zheng, Christopher Monroe, Jacob P. Covey
abstract: Rydberg-based two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral atom arrays are limited chiefly by laser intensity inhomogeneity and by detuning errors from frequency miscalibration, background-field drift, intermediate state light shift and Doppler shifts. Quantum optimal control can suppress the former, but no pulse can render a controlled-Z gate first-order insensitive to detuning. Here we show that this obstruction can be circumvented by designing Rydberg gate pulses with every leading-order detuning error relegated to single-qubit Z-rotations, which an echoed sequence removes. The resulting maximally-entangling ZZ gate has no leading-order response to arbitrary detunings on either atom, maintaining an infidelity below $10^{-3}$ much wider range of single-atom detunings than previous gate designs. We further show that a large fraction of residual error is dominated by population outside the computational subspace, which can be converted into heralded erasures. Our results significantly reduce the requirements on laser frequency stability and intensity homogeneity, field calibration and atomic temperature toward practical fault-tolerant quantum computing with neutral atoms.
summary: This paper presents a novel, detuning-robust scheme for implementing two-qubit entangling gates using Rydberg atoms in neutral atom arrays. By designing specialized, echoed pulse sequences, the authors circumvent fundamental limitations in gate design, achieving high fidelity even when the laser frequency or intensity deviates significantly from the ideal calibration point. This significantly improves the feasibility of using neutral atoms for practical, fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_problem: The primary challenge is designing Rydberg entangling gates that are robust to detuning errors, overcoming the theoretical limitation that no simple pulse can make a controlled-Z gate first-order insensitive to detuning.
main_result: The authors propose an echoed pulse sequence that achieves a maximally-entangling ZZ gate with no leading-order response to arbitrary detunings, maintaining high fidelity ($<10^{-3}$) over a wide detuning range.
method: The method involves using quantum optimal control and perturbation theory to design pulse shapes that cancel out leading-order detuning errors, supplemented by an echo sequence to remove residual single-qubit phase errors.
model_or_system: The system utilizes neutral atoms trapped in optical tweezer arrays, employing Rydberg states to mediate two-qubit interactions. The analysis involves modeling the Hamiltonian under various detuning conditions ($\Delta_1, \Delta_2$) and optimizing the pulse sequence.
key_observables: Gate fidelity ($F$), infidelity as a function of detuning ($\Delta$), and the residual Rydberg population leakage.
important_parameters: Detuning ($\Delta$), Rabi frequency ($\Omega$), and the ratio of detuning to Rabi frequency ($\Delta/\Omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on first-order perturbation theory, and it assumes that residual Rydberg population leakage can be converted into heralded erasures for fault-tolerant analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the level scheme and circuit diagram for the gate, showing error channels under various detunings. Other figures compare simulated gate infidelity for different pulse types (TO vs. ADR/DR) across detuning ranges and show the physical constraints on pulse shaping (modulation frequency).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the detuning robustness problem to developing the theoretical framework using perturbation theory and optimal control. It details the specific pulse sequence (echoed $\sqrt{CZ}$) and analyzes its performance under symmetric, anti-symmetric, and arbitrary detunings, concluding with discussions on physical constraints like bandwidth.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the practical limitations of implementing quantum gates using neutral atoms, providing concrete pulse engineering techniques to enhance robustness against common experimental imperfections like frequency drift and intensity inhomogeneity.
